newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF says not yet ready to hand over Russia cash.
newsitem.headline: IMF says not yet ready to hand over Russia cash.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund is not yet ready to recommend releasing a new tranche of its $10 billion three-year loan to Russia, but experts will return soon to Moscow for further talks, the IMF Moscow representative said on Tuesday.
"The mission is not yet in a position to recommend the release of the latest tranche," Martin Gilman told Reuters. The monitoring mission left Moscow last Friday.
Gilman said the IMF mission had returned to Washington for consultations. But reports in Russian newspapers that the IMF had frozen its Russia loan were not true.
He said issues to be finalised included "Russia's revenue projections for this year as a whole, the integrity of the fiscal programme as well as some aspects of structural reform".

The IMF delayed two tranches of the loan in the final quarter of last year, complaining Russia was not collecting enough tax to meet its budget plans. But the experts relented earlier this month, releasing almost $650 million and praising Russia for "several important structural reform measures".
Analysts said they expected the loan tranche to be approved once the IMF received more data on the Russian economy and its likely performance this year.
